result.title: probe: both-filter twins and default pull_request types (throwaway, do not merge)
result.body:
Scratch probe for #363 (a trigger setting both a filter and its `-ignore` twin) and #365 (`DEFAULT_TYPES`).

Four independent workflows:

- `both-branches.yml` — `branches: [main]` AND `branches-ignore: [main]`, jobs `bb-a`/`bb-b`
- `both-paths.yml` — `paths: ['**']` AND `paths-ignore: ['**']`, jobs `bp-a`/`bp-b`
- `d-default.yml` — bare `on: pull_request:`
- `d-labeled.yml` — `types: [labeled]`

Procedure: read the dispatched list on `opened`, then apply a label and read it again on `labeled`. Closed unmerged once captured; the closed PR is the permanent record.

Do not merge. Do not arm auto-merge.

commit.message:
Capture case P7: a draft PR marked ready for review (#371)

Scratch PR #358 carried a workflow declaring
`types: [ready_for_review]` alongside one with default types. Opening it
as a draft fired `opened`; marking it ready fired `ready_for_review` on
the same head SHA.

The ready transition dispatched `p7-ready` and nothing else — no
default-`types:` workflow re-ran, `pull_request_target` included. The
case declares its action in `action.json`; the prediction matches.

The capture recipe assumed one dispatch per head SHA, so it now says how
to partition a SHA that carries two.

release: skip

files.patch:
@@ -102,6 +102,13 @@ gh api "repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs" \
 
 `fixture.json` is those job names, deduplicated and sorted.
 
+One head SHA can carry more than one dispatch: a draft PR marked ready fires
+`opened` and then `ready_for_review` on the same commit. A prediction answers
+one event, so the fixture is the runs that event produced, not the union.
+The runs API reports no activity type, so partition by workflow `.path` —
+each file's `types:` says which action could have dispatched it — and
+corroborate with `created_at`. Name the action in `action.json`.
+
 ### Re-record, never edit
 
 A hand-edited fixture asserts what someone believed GitHub would answer. Re-run

@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+A workflow declaring `types: [ready_for_review]`, dispatched by marking a
+draft pull request ready.
+
+Head SHA `8722f52` carries two dispatches. Opening the draft fired `opened`
+and produced `CI Gate` (pr-monitor.yml), `p7-default` (default `types:`) and
+`prt-noop` (`pull_request_target`). Marking the PR ready fired
+`ready_for_review` and produced only `p7-ready`; nothing with default `types:`
+re-ran, `pull_request_target` included. This fixture is the second dispatch,
+named by `action.json`.

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+Scratch PR #358, opened as a draft and then marked ready for review, closed
+unmerged after both dispatches concluded.

name: putitoutthere check

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'putitoutthere.toml'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'scripts/*/package.json'
      - '.github/workflows/release.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/check.yml'

jobs:
  putitoutthere-check:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/check.yml@v0

name: Testing Conventions (willfire)

# Runs the upstream testing-conventions gates over the root `willfire` package,
# pinned to the rolling `v0` tag (the same convention as check.yml).
#
# Every gate runs (`gates` left at its empty default): mutation's Stryker deps
# are in devDependencies, and `e2e-attestations/` holds the receipt the
# e2e-verify gate checks.
#
# One workflow file per workspace package (docs/monorepo.md), because `paths:`
# is per-file and each package's lane has a different trigger set.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'e2e-attestations/**'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
      - 'tsconfig.json'
      - 'tsconfig.build.json'
      - 'vitest.config.mts'
      - '.github/workflows/conventions-src.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'e2e-attestations/**'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
      - 'tsconfig.json'
      - 'tsconfig.build.json'
      - 'vitest.config.mts'
      - '.github/workflows/conventions-src.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Job id kept as-is: it prefixes every check name this call produces.
  conventions:
    uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml@v0
    with:
      languages: '["typescript"]'
      source: src

on:

name: integration

# The suite builds `src` and replays `tests/integration`, importing
# `tests/cases.ts` and `tests/getResponse.ts`; `attestations.test.ts` reads
# `e2e-attestations/`. `tests/e2e` and `tests/fixtures` are read by no CI job.
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/integration/**'
      - 'tests/cases.ts'
      - 'tests/getResponse.ts'
      - 'e2e-attestations/**'
      - 'tsconfig.json'
      - 'tsconfig.build.json'
      - 'vitest.config.mts'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'pnpm-lock.yaml'
      - 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'
      - '.github/workflows/integration.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  integration:
    name: integration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm test:integration

name: PR Monitor

on:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  monitor:
    name: 'CI Gate'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The action has no timeout of its own (see monitor.ts) — this is the
    # backstop. If a predicted run never dispatches, the gate waits here
    # until the job is killed.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: thekevinscott/pr-monitor@v1

name: prt-noop

# Permanent probe for case D13 (#328): pull_request_target is read from the
# default branch, so the only way a prediction of it can be exercised is a
# workflow that lives here forever.
on:
  pull_request_target:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  prt-noop:
    name: prt-noop
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - run: 'true'

name: Release

# putitoutthere's reusable workflow; config lives in `putitoutthere.toml`
# at the repo root.
#
# Auth: the `NPM_TOKEN` secret is the first-publish bootstrap only —
# Trusted Publishing on npm binds to an already-published package, so
# the very first publish has no OIDC path. `willfire` is published:
# register the trusted publisher (repo thekevinscott/willfire,
# workflow release.yml, environment release), then DELETE the NPM_TOKEN
# secret; the OIDC exchange takes over.
#
# Filename matters: npm's trust policy matches the caller workflow
# filename. Renaming this file requires re-registering the trusted
# publisher.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_packages:
        description: >
          Packages to release manually, bypassing change detection.
          Comma-separated list of name[@<bump|version>] entries, e.g.
          "willfire@minor" or "willfire@1.2.0". Leave empty to fall back
          to automatic change detection (same as a push).
        required: false
        default: ''

jobs:
  release:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    with:
      release_packages: ${{ inputs.release_packages || '' }}
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # Required even for the token-auth bootstrap publish: the
      # reusable workflow's publish job declares id-token: write, and
      # a caller granting less is a startup error.
      id-token: write

  # PyPI upload runs in the caller's workflow context (see
  # pypi/warehouse#11096). The `if:` gate skips this job for non-PyPI
  # repos — pasted verbatim per putitoutthere's README regardless of
  # what the repo publishes.
  pypi-publish:
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.has_pypi == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: dist/
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

name: typecheck

on:

name: unit

# `src/` reaches 100% from its colocated tests, so the integration suite is
# not propping the number up.

concurrency:

permissions:

jobs:

    name: unit (100% coverage)

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm test:unit
